Optimal.Notes: A locked 40 fps at 40 Hz feels smooth and is well-matched to the Deck LCD; medium textures and view distance give a good-looking world without overwhelming the RDNA 2 GPU. Drop Shadow Distance to Low if horde nights cause dips.

profiles.Summary: 7 Days to Die is a demanding open-world survival game that runs on the Steam Deck via Proton at playable but modest frame rates; expect 30–45 fps depending on settings, with voxel-based world generation and zombie hordes being the primary performance bottlenecks. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support, though the open-world nature and Unity engine mean performance varies significantly between exploration and horde nights.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (GTX 1050 Ti class) against 7 Days to Die's Unity engine demands. On your first run, check fps during a horde night and in a city POI — those are the hardest scenarios — and step down to the Optimal or Max Battery profile if the frame rate dips below your target.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at sub-native with FSR upscaling and a locked 30 fps cap at 40 Hz refresh keeps the APU well within the 8 W TDP envelope; expect dips during horde nights. Lowering View Distance is the single biggest performance lever in this game.

KnownIssues: Horde nights and large zombie groups can cause significant frame drops below 30 fps even at low settings.
Chunk loading during fast travel or exploration can cause stutters as new terrain generates.
ProtonDB trending gold (not platinum) suggests occasional Proton-related issues; GE-Proton may improve stability.
Small UI text and menus can be difficult to read at 1280x800 without UI scaling adjustments.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Native resolution at full TDP targets 60 fps but the open world and zombie hordes will realistically pull averages into the 40–55 range; consider dropping the frame cap to 40 if stutters appear during horde nights. Battery life is short at this profile — best used plugged in or for short sessions.

Optimal.Notes: Locking to 40 fps at 40 Hz gives a smooth, tear-free experience that suits the slower-paced exploration and building gameplay; FSR at 1024x640 recovers enough GPU headroom to keep quality settings at medium. Drop View Distance further if frame rate dips during Blood Moon horde nights.
